summary: Climber fell on the final pitch of a technical climb on Lone Eagle Peak and sustained serious injuries; Flight For Life located the pair and a Buckley Black Hawk helicopter with Rocky Mountain Rescue hoisted the patient before sunset
location: Lone Eagle Peak, Indian Peaks Wilderness
responding_agency: Grand County SAR, Flight For Life, Buckley AFB Black Hawk, Rocky Mountain Rescue
notes: Merged duplicate legacy-003648 after maintainer confirmation on 2026-09-24. DATE UNCERTAIN: legacy-003648 records 2018-07-01 from Grand County SAR Facebook posts; legacy-000537 inferred 2018-07-02 from a July 3 article quoting a GCSAR post saying yesterday. The quoted post may predate the article, so that inference is not conclusive. Retained 2018-07-02 provisionally for continuity; exact incident date needs verification against the original agency post. County Grand and GCSAR response added from the duplicate and corroborated by the incident narratives. The three agency post URLs and both existing article URLs are retained. CSAR narrative (coloradosar.org): GCSAR paged just before 2:00 PM on multiple SPOT distress activations; subject a 52-year-old experienced climber who fell ~20 ft plus a 10-20 ft roll ten feet above his last protection on a ten-pitch route on the north face near Monarch Lake, with suspected head/back/rib injuries; mission leader Greg Foley + CSAR coordinator Bruce Fosdick (Douglas County SAR) requested a Buckley Black Hawk on standby, dispatched six RMRG members to Boulder Airport, and had FFL Lifeguard 1 fly over (Lifeguard 2 later stood by); a GCSAR ground team hiked in from Monarch Lake; the Black Hawk hoisted the patient on the fourth attempt in 30-mph gusts and landed at Granby Airport ~8:30 PM, transferring him to FFL for a Denver hospital.
